title: Stonebridge Bank - Data Residency & Compliance Discovery
summary: Initial discovery on data residency, logging restrictions, and compliance posture for potential Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment. Customer requires EU data residency for EU customers, strict logging retention controls, SOC2/ISO evidence, and option for on-prem or VPC Private deployment for sensitive workloads. Agreed next step: send SOC2/ISO reports, security architecture doc, and schedule a benchmark/POC for dedicated instance with sample dataset.
topics: HIPAA considerations for financial services (PII handling)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
KMS/HSM and encryption at rest/in transit
next_steps: Maya to share SOC 2 and ISO 27001 reports and security architecture doc by 2026-03-06
Tom to propose POC plan and required dataset/ingest checklist by 2026-03-09
Customer to confirm list of EU vs US workloads and retention policy by 2026-03-11
Schedule technical benchmark week of 2026-03-16 (Tom + Ethan + Mark)

Tom: prepare POC runbook and sampling/ingest checklist (due 2026-03-09)

transcription:
00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya Patel from Redwood, AE on this account. Tom Reynolds, our solutions engineer, is with me. how are you all?
00:06 Anna (Stonebridge CISO): Hi Maya, thanks. I'm Anna Lopez, CISO, Priya Shah is here for compliance and Mark Ritter from infra. Ethan from ML platform joining.
00:15 Maya: Great. We put this call together to understand your requirements around data residency and logging - especially for EU customers and any high-risk flows. Quick agenda: current stack, rules on logging and retention, compliance requirements (SOC2/ISO, GDPR, HIPAA considerations), and deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private).
00:30 Mark: Sounds good. For context, we run multi-region services, EU customer data must remain in EU and we have strict logging limitations - for certain flows we cannot persist full request payloads for more than 30 days and some fields are not allowed to be logged at all.
00:45 Tom (Redwood SE): Thanks, that's helpful. A couple clarifying q's up front: when you say "EU data must remain in EU", do you mean both at-rest and processing must happen in EU regions, and no logs or backups may leave the EU?
00:55 Priya (Compliance): Correct. Processing and storage within EU. Backups also must be within EU. We also need controls for access to logs - only certain roles, encryption keys managed in our KMS.
01:05 Maya: Understood. We typically offer three modes: Redwood Hosted (our hosted API with region pinning), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity running in a customer-dedicated cluster in a chosen cloud region), and Redwood Private (either VPC-hosted with private control plane or on-prem). Each has different guarantees around isolation and data flow.
01:22 Mark: Can you walk through what Hosted actually means for residency? We've seen vendors claim region pinning, but logs or telemetry sometimes still go back to the vendor region.
01:32 Tom: Good question. For Hosted we can configure region pinning so inference runs in e.g. eu-west-1. However, some vendor-level telemetry and aggregated metrics can cross regions depending on the control plane. For strict EU-only requirements we usually recommend Dedicated with customer-owned VPC peering or Private deployment. We do offer an EU-hosted tenancy option with contractual guarantees for certain customers, but there are limits around debug logs and vendor-managed telemetry.
01:55 Anna: That aligns with our risk model. For some regulated products we may need total control - prefer Private or Dedicated. Also curious about logging redaction - can we prevent full request bodies from being logged or redact fields?
02:07 Tom: Yes. We have request-level logging controls and field redaction; you can specify a retention period and a schema-based scrubber to redact PII before logs persist. For Dedicated and Private you get more granular control - ability to disable logging entirely for certain routes and to retain logs in your own storage.
02:22 Priya: And how about audit logs? We need immutable audit trails for access to keys and admin actions - and proof of where data was processed.
02:31 Maya: We support audit logs with write-once retention policies. For Dedicated/Private we can ship logs to your S3/GCS buckets within the EU and set lifecycle rules. We also integrate with your KMS/HSM for admin key ops and can log key-access events to your SIEM.
02:45 Mark: Encryption in transit & at rest? We use customer-managed keys for encryption at rest for our core DBs - we'd prefer Redwood to use our KMS as well for any persisted artifacts.
02:55 Tom: For Private and Dedicated you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) or HSM. Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys, but for enterprise plans we support customer KMS. We'll need to detail specifics in the architecture doc.
03:12 Anna: HIPAA - not primary but some of our partners touch healthcare data occasionally. Do you sign BAA and support the controls required?
03:20 Maya: We do sign a BAA for covered healthcare data. We have encryption, access controls, and logging features that align to HIPAA administrative safeguards. We'll share our security compliance pack.
03:29 Priya: GDPR-wise, we need processors and subprocessors list, DPA, and SCCs or adequacy. Also data subject request support - ability to locate and delete a customer's conversations.
03:40 Maya: We'll provide DPA and subprocessors list; SCCs are supported. For deletion, Redwood supports per-customer data deletion and retention rules; for Hosted we can delete on request but it's important to confirm where backups may reside. For Dedicated/Private you have full control and can ensure no vendor backups.
03:57 Mark: We also want to avoid long-term storage of KV cache for low-risk requests; is KV cache persisted outside of ephemeral GPU instances?
04:05 Tom: By default KV caches are kept in-memory for serving; for scale we use a managed cache that may persist short-term. For Dedicated/Private we can keep cache in ephemeral nodes or in your managed redis in the same region, which ensures residency.
04:18 Ethan (ML Platform): On model variants and rollbacks - if you do a fallback to a cheaper variant, does that move data to a different region? We need to make sure fallbacks respect region constraints.
04:28 Tom: Fallbacks are policy-driven. We can restrict variants to the same region or restrict fallbacks by tier. We'll show the routing policy config in the POC.
04:36 Anna: Logging restriction example: for some flows we need the request text stripped immediately and only metadata retained for 30 days. Can Redwood support route-level logging policies?
04:45 Tom: Yes, route-level policies exist. You can set logging to "none", "metadata-only", or "full" per route. You can also plug in a pre-ingest redactor to remove or hash fields.
04:55 Priya: We have an internal compliance rule: for EU customers, even aggregated metrics cannot leave the EU. Is that feasible?
05:03 Maya: For full EU-only metrics flow we recommend Dedicated in an EU region or Private VPC. For Hosted we can mill partial guarantees but telemetry may transit for platform observability; we can set up log export directly to your EU buckets to minimize vendor transfer.
05:18 Mark: What about certifications? We need SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001, penetration test reports, and a recent architecture review.
05:27 Maya: We have SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001. We'll send our pen test summary (redacted) and architecture/security whitepaper.
05:36 Anna: Any known customers in financial services with similar constraints?
05:40 Maya: Yes, multiple regional banks using Dedicated and Private. We can provide redacted references and a brief case study.
05:47 Ethan: Regarding PII minimization - does Redwood offer built-in embedding scrubbers or differential privacy features?
05:55 Tom: We have content filters and taxonomy-based scrubbers; differential privacy isn't a default but we can discuss approaches for sensitive analytics. For embeddings we recommend tokenization and PII masking pre-embed.
06:06 Mark: For the POC we'd like a performance benchmark on typical request sizes - concurrency 50-100, avg tokens 120, max 800, latency 200-300ms SLO for synchronous flows. Is that achievable on Dedicated?
06:18 Tom: Yes, Dedicated can be tuned. We'll propose batch sizing and kernel/quantization profiles; for your SLOs we'll run a benchmark with recommended instance types. We'll scope the exact GPU type in the POC plan.
06:29 Priya: Legal/procurement - contract clauses around data residency, audit, and right to inspect are needed. Procurement will expect to see our DPA modifications.
06:37 Maya: Understood. We'll surface the DPA and common contract redlines. For Private deployments we have an enterprise licensing model that covers on-prem options.
06:46 Anna: Are there limitations on data egress if we want to keep logs in our S3 in the EU but have the control plane in US?
06:53 Tom: If control plane in US, metadata may cross; we can negotiate a private control plane for enterprise customers to keep control plane in EU. For strict residency, keep control plane and data plane in same region.
07:05 Maya: Quick recap: you need EU data processing + backups in EU, strict logging controls and redaction, BYOK for keys, SOC2/ISO docs, and a POC with benchmarks. We'll send security docs and POC runbook, and arrange benchmark.
07:18 Mark: That covers it. One last question - does Redwood retain conversation logs for model training? We need assurance that no training on customer data occurs unless explicitly opted in.
07:28 Maya: We do not use customer data for training by default. There are options to opt-in for improvement, but enterprise contracts can explicitly prohibit training data use.
07:36 Priya: Great. Let's capture next steps and owners.
07:40 Maya: I'll send the SOC2/ISO pack and architecture doc by Friday (2026-03-06). Tom will prepare POC runbook and sample dataset checklist. Priya please share retention policy and data classification. Mark to provide region list and access for benchmark. We'll tentatively plan the benchmark week of 2026-03-16.
07:55 Anna: Thanks, everyone. We'll review and coordinate procurement/legal next week.
08:00 Maya: Thanks all, talk soon.

Notes: occasional transcription noise - "K V cache" written as KV, "SAML" was transcribed correctly but there were a couple instances where vendor names were slightly off. References to attachments: Maya mentioned sending "SOC2 pack" and "architecture whitepaper" (links to be sent), Tom to share POC doc (link).
